cases.question: Which cache approach is justified for the current workload?
cases.constraints: Eight concurrent writers; reliability matters more than minimum code.

evidence.text: Cachepolicy: I recommend A, an in-process cache. This advice assumes a single-process toy workload.
The workload now has eight concurrent writers. I recommend B, a coordinated shared cache, for that requirement. Neither option has been benchmarked in the current environment.

cases.question: Which retry policy is supported by the available check?
cases.constraints: Use only the result for synthetic revision demo-r2 and the two-second deadline.

evidence.text: Retrypolicy: A, unlimited retry, should recover reliably. I recommend it. No measurements attached.

Observed fixture check bounded-retry, revision demo-r2, environment synthetic single-worker: A exceeded the two-second deadline; B (bounded retries) completed within it. This corrects the earlier unlimited-retry recommendation. Only this scenario was tested.

cases.question: Which storage option is better supported for the reopen requirement?
cases.constraints: Reopen correctness on synthetic revision demo-r3; no claim about throughput.

evidence.text: Storagepolicy: use A. I am very confident A is best. No test output is attached.
I recommend B for reopen correctness, but my recommendation alone is not a test result.

Observed fixture check reopen, revision demo-r3, environment synthetic local process: A lost the last committed entry after reopening; B retained it. This check measured reopen correctness only, not speed or scale.
